events.title: Early Civilizations
events.description: Bronze Age civilizations emerged in Afghanistan region. Located on Silk Road, it became crossroads of Eastern and Western civilizations.

events.title: Persian Achaemenid Empire Rule
events.description: Persian Empire controlled Afghanistan, incorporating it into Bactria province. Persian culture profoundly influenced Afghanistan.

events.title: Alexander the Great's Conquest
events.description: Alexander the Great entered Afghanistan after conquering Persia, establishing multiple cities. Greek culture entered, forming Greco-Bactrian civilization.

events.title: Greco-Bactrian Kingdom
events.description: Greeks established Bactrian Kingdom in Afghanistan, Greek culture flourished in Central Asia.

events.title: Kushan Empire
events.description: Kushan Empire controlled Afghanistan and today's Pakistan region, promoting East-West trade. Buddhism flourished here, Bamiyan Buddhas and other Buddhist sites constructed.

events.title: Arab Muslim Conquest
events.description: Arab Caliphate conquered Afghanistan, Islam entered and gradually replaced Buddhism, becoming main religion.

events.title: Samanid Dynasty
events.description: Persian Samanid dynasty ruled Afghanistan, Persian culture and Islamic civilization flourished.

events.title: Ghaznavid Dynasty
events.description: Ghaznavid dynasty centered on Afghan Ghazni, built powerful empire. Sultan Mahmud repeatedly invaded India, plundering wealth.

events.title: Mongol Invasion
events.description: Genghis Khan and Mongol armies invaded Afghanistan, massively destroying cities. Herat and other cities suffered devastating blows.

events.title: Timurid Empire
events.description: Timur built empire, capital Samarkand, ruling Central Asia including Afghanistan. Herat became cultural center.

events.title: Persian and Mughal Contest
events.description: Afghanistan became contested object between Persian Safavid dynasty and Indian Mughal Empire, changing hands multiple times.

events.title: Durrani Dynasty Established (Modern Afghanistan Born)
events.description: Ahmad Shah Durrani established the Durrani Dynasty, unifying Afghan tribes and founding the Afghan state. He is revered as 'Father of Afghanistan.'

events.title: 'Great Game' Era
events.description: Afghanistan became focus of British and Russian struggle for Central Asian control. Afghanistan survived in gap between two great empires.

events.title: First Anglo-Afghan War
events.description: Britain invaded Afghanistan, attempting to install a pro-British regime. Afghan tribes fiercely resisted, British forces suffered devastating defeat and retreat. This was one of Britain's worst colonial defeats.

events.title: Second Anglo-Afghan War
events.description: Britain invaded Afghanistan again. After war signed Treaty of Gandamak, Afghanistan ceded some territory, foreign affairs controlled by Britain.

events.title: Third Anglo-Afghan War and Independence
events.description: King Amanullah Khan launched independence war, repelling British forces. Britain recognized Afghanistan's complete independence. August 19 became Afghanistan Independence Day.

events.title: Amanullah Khan's Modernization Reforms
events.description: Amanullah Khan implemented radical modernization and secularization reforms, including women's rights, education, dress. But reforms too rapid triggered conservative rebellion, king overthrown.

events.title: Civil War and Bacha-i-Saqao's Brief Rule
events.description: Tajik warlord Bacha-i-Saqao (bandit) briefly captured Kabul, ruling for 9 months. Afghanistan fell into chaos.

events.title: Nadir Shah Restores Order
events.description: Nadir Shah defeated Bacha-i-Saqao, restored order and became king. But he was assassinated in 1933.

events.title: King Zahir Shah's Rule
events.description: King Zahir Shah ruled for 40 years, a relatively peaceful and stable period for Afghanistan. 1960s implemented 'democracy experiment', Kabul became cultural center.

events.title: Kabul's Golden Age
events.description: This period was called Kabul's Golden Age. Women enjoyed education and work rights, cities modernized, called 'Paris of Asia'.

events.title: New Constitution and Democratic Reforms
events.description: King Zahir promulgated new constitution, established parliamentary system, allowed political parties (except communists and Islamic extremists). This was Afghanistan's democratic experiment.

events.title: Daoud Coup
events.description: Former Prime Minister Mohammed Daoud launched coup, overthrowing King Zahir, abolishing monarchy, establishing Republic of Afghanistan.

events.title: Saur Revolution (Communist Coup)
events.description: People's Democratic Party of Afghanistan (communist party) launched coup, overthrowing Daoud government. Communists began ruling, implementing radical socialist reforms.

events.title: Soviet Invasion of Afghanistan
events.description: Soviet Union deployed 100,000 troops to invade Afghanistan, supporting communist regime. This triggered a 10-year Afghan War, becoming 'Soviet Union's Vietnam.'

events.title: Soviet-Afghan War and Mujahideen Resistance
events.description: Afghan mujahideen fought Soviet forces with US, Pakistani, and Saudi support. War killed about 1.5 million Afghans, with 5 million refugees fleeing to Pakistan and Iran.

events.title: Soviet Withdrawal
events.description: Soviet Union admitted defeat, withdrew all troops. About 15,000 Soviet soldiers killed in war. This accelerated Soviet Union's dissolution.

events.title: Najibullah Government
events.description: Soviet-backed Najibullah government continued ruling, but difficult to sustain after Soviet withdrawal and aid cessation.

events.title: Civil War and Warlord Fighting
events.description: After mujahideen overthrew Najibullah government, various factions engaged in civil war, fighting for power. Kabul suffered severe destruction, tens of thousands of civilians died.

events.title: Taliban Emerges
events.description: Taliban movement led by Mullah Omar emerged in Kandahar, promising to restore order and implement Sharia law. Taliban rapidly expanded.

events.title: Taliban Captures Kabul
events.description: Taliban captured Kabul, establishing 'Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan.' They imposed extreme Islamic rule, banning music, television, and severely restricting women's rights.

events.title: Destruction of Bamiyan Buddhas
events.description: Taliban defied international protests, destroying 1,500-year-old Bamiyan Buddhas, a massive loss to world cultural heritage.

events.title: Massoud Assassinated
events.description: Anti-Taliban leader Ahmad Shah Massoud ('Lion of Panjshir') assassinated by Al-Qaeda assassins, two days before 9/11.

events.title: US Invasion of Afghanistan
events.description: After 9/11, US invaded Afghanistan, citing Taliban harboring bin Laden. US forces allied with Northern Alliance, quickly overthrew Taliban regime.

events.title: Civil War and Warlord Chaos
events.description: After Soviet-backed government fell, mujahideen factions fought for power. Kabul was devastated by civil war, tens of thousands died. Warlords ruled, Afghanistan fell into darkest period.

events.title: Bonn Agreement and Karzai Interim Government
events.description: Afghan factions reached agreement in Bonn, establishing interim government. Hamid Karzai appointed interim chairman.

events.title: Karzai Elected President
events.description: Afghanistan held first democratic presidential election, Karzai elected. New constitution promulgated, Islamic Republic of Afghanistan established.

events.title: US Occupation and Taliban Insurgency
events.description: US and NATO forces stationed in Afghanistan for 20 years, supporting Afghan government against Taliban insurgency. War killed about 240,000 (including about 70,000 civilians), US spent over $2 trillion.

events.title: Bin Laden Killed
events.description: US forces killed bin Laden in Pakistan. Though not in Afghanistan, this was symbolic victory in war on terror.

events.title: Ashraf Ghani Elected President
events.description: Ghani elected president in controversial election. He led government against Taliban, but faced serious corruption and inefficiency problems.

events.title: US-Taliban Peace Agreement
events.description: US and Taliban signed peace agreement in Doha, Qatar, US promised withdrawal, Taliban promised not to let Afghanistan become terrorist base.

events.title: US Begins Withdrawal
events.description: US and NATO forces began withdrawing, transferring security responsibility to Afghan government. Taliban regained strength, conflict continued.

events.title: Taliban All-Out Offensive
events.description: After US withdrawal, Taliban rapidly captured territory. Afghan government forces barely resisted, multiple provincial capitals fell.

events.title: Kabul Falls and Taliban Retake Power
events.description: Taliban captured Kabul without fight, President Ghani fled to UAE. Islamic Republic of Afghanistan collapsed, Taliban retook power after 20 years, reestablishing 'Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan.'

events.title: Kabul Airport Chaotic Evacuation
events.description: Tens of thousands of Afghans rushed to Kabul airport, attempting to flee Taliban rule. Chaos included suicide bomb attack, killing about 170. Scenes of US hasty withdrawal shocked the world.

events.title: Panjshir Resistance Fails
events.description: Ahmad Massoud (son of Massoud) organized resistance in Panjshir Valley, but defeated by Taliban. Taliban completely controlled Afghanistan.

events.title: Taliban Second Rule
events.description: Taliban reimposed Sharia law, severely restricting women's rights (banning girls from secondary school and university, banning women from work). International community refuses to recognize Taliban regime, Afghanistan faces severe humanitarian crisis.

events.title: Humanitarian Disaster
events.description: Under Taliban rule, Afghan economy collapsed, millions face starvation, women's rights regressed. International aid drastically reduced, about 2/3 of 39 million population need humanitarian aid. Afghanistan became world's most oppressive country toward women.

events.title: 塔利班鞏固統治
events.description: 塔利班持續統治，實行嚴格的伊斯蘭教法。婦女被排除在公共生活之外，經濟停滯，但塔利班控制穩固。國際社會繼續拒絕承認政權。...
